english: what have you got to do with …?
also: what do you have to do with him?
what business is it of yours?

terms.gloss: what have you to do with him?
terms.grammar: question without a verb: quid with the dative of the person and cum with the ablative
evidence: Ter. Eun. 3.3.4: Quid tibi cum illā? (Lewis & Short), s.v. tum
Sen. Ep. 15.10: quid tibi cum cēterīs?
terms.comment: The dative is the person asked, cum the person or thing he has dealings with; est is left out.

terms.gloss: what business have you with him?
terms.grammar: reī, partitive genitive; Plautus has commercī in the same frame
evidence: Plaut. Aul. 4.4.4: quid tibi mēcum est commercī, senex? (Lewis & Short), s.v. commercium

phrases.latin: quid tibi cum cēterīs? tē ipse antecessistī
phrases.english: what do you care about the others? you’ve beaten yourself

sources: Lewis & Short: cum · Lewis & Short: commercium
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 100, 326.
Sen. Ep. 15.10 from the Latinitas loci collection (loci-seneca-epistulae), checked against the edition named there.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
